readme.html:
Fireball

A small dodge game for the Game Boy Advance, written in C. Saahil Sanganeriya built it in spring 2022 for Georgia Tech's CS 2110 (Computer Organization and Programming), homework 8: a Mode 3 program that draws with DMA, waits for VBlank, reads the buttons and detects collisions.

How to play

You are the smiley face. Fireballs bounce around the screen. Touch a lit fireball and the game is over. Last until the timer reaches the goal and you win. Pick the mode on the title screen.

Mode Button Fireballs Speed per axis (pixels per frame) Goal
Easy A 2 1 10 s (600 frames)
Medium B 5 1 or 2 25 s (1,500 frames)
Hard R 8, of which 7 light 1 to 4 40 s (2,400 frames)
  • One fireball lights at the start and another every 6 seconds (360 frames). Until it lights, a fireball moves but is invisible and harmless. On Hard, the eighth would light at 42 s, after the 40 s goal, so it never appears.
  • Each fireball starts at a random place, moving down and to the right, and bounces off the edges of the screen.
  • The bottom-left corner shows the seconds survived and the goal.
  • The D-pad moves you one pixel per frame. Select goes back to the title screen from the game, the win screen or the game-over screen.

These values are in main.c: modes at lines 62–78, speeds at line 45, the 6-second step at line 143.

Keys in mGBA

GBA button mGBA default key CS 2110 course key (printed on the title screen)
A (Easy) X Z
B (Medium) Z X
R (Hard) S S
Select (back to title) Backspace Backspace
D-pad arrow keys arrow keys

The title screen uses the course's mGBA key set-up. With mGBA's own defaults the keys for A and B are the other way round: press X for Easy and Z for Medium.

Build and run

The Makefile is the CS 2110 course Makefile. It includes /opt/cs2110-tools/GBAVariables.mak, which comes with the course's Docker image, together with the ARM cross-compiler and mGBA. Inside that container:

make        # builds App.gba
make mgba   # builds App.gba and opens it in mGBA
make clean  # removes build output

App.gba then runs in any Game Boy Advance emulator, such as mGBA. No ROM is committed.

Outside the course container the Makefile does not run, because the included file is missing. Another GBA toolchain, such as devkitARM, needs its own Makefile; that has not been tried. CMakeLists.txt only lets an IDE (CLion) index the code. It compiles for the host computer, not for the GBA.

How it works

  • One loop, five states. main.c runs a state machine: START (title, pick a mode), STARTBG (place the player and the fireballs), GAMEPLAY, then WON or GAMEOVER, and back to START on Select.
  • Frame timing. waitForVBlank() in gba.c polls the scanline counter until the screen enters VBlank (line 160) and counts the frame. The game's clock is that count: 60 frames are shown as one second.
  • Drawing. The screen is Mode 3: a 240 × 160 bitmap of 15-bit colours in video memory. Every frame the game clears the screen with DMA, draws the lit fireballs and the player with DMA, one row at a time, and writes the timer text pixel by pixel.
  • Collisions. The player (20 × 20) and each lit fireball (10 × 10) are boxes; any overlap ends the game.
  • Images. The PNGs in images/ were converted to C arrays with nin10kit. The three full-screen images are 76,800 bytes each (START_SIZE, GAMEOVER_SIZE, WON_SIZE in images/*.h), most of the game's data.

TECHNICAL_OVERVIEW.md walks through the code in more detail.

Files

File What it is Written by
main.c, main.h the game: state machine, player and fireballs Saahil, on the course's skeleton
gba.c VBlank wait, pixel and DMA drawing Saahil wrote the VBlank wait and the pixel and DMA drawing functions; the text-drawing and random-number helpers came with the course files
gba.h GBA register, button and DMA definitions CS 2110 starter code
font.c 6 × 8 pixel font for the timer text CS 2110 starter code
Makefile build rules CS 2110 starter code, unchanged
images/ title, game-over and win screens, player and fireball sprites, as PNG and as nin10kit C arrays garbage.* is the course's example image; the game does not draw it
CMakeLists.txt IDE project file
TECHNICAL_OVERVIEW.md longer notes on the code

Credits and licence

The CS 2110 course staff (spring 2022) wrote the starter files: gba.h, font.c, the Makefile, the skeletons of main.c and main.h, the text-drawing and random-number helpers in gba.c, and images/garbage.*. Images were converted with nin10kit.
